nodes.label: ACK
nodes.rationale: The core primitive of reliable delivery: the producer frees a buffered message once it is acked. Fire-and-forget from controller to the producer's replyTo — the controller does not wait for delivery, so the handler pays no latency for it, and a lost ACK is recovered by the producer's retransmit plus the controller's dedup-and-re-ACK.

nodes.label: Handler contract (resolve acks, throw retransmits)
nodes.rationale: The handler is the only user-facing switch; dedup, ACK, replyTo wiring and retransmit timing belong to the controller. Catching an error inside the handler is the trap — a clean resolve acks a message whose processing failed, so let exceptions propagate or persist the failure for a separate retry workflow.

nodes.label: Persist before resolve
nodes.rationale: Awaiting the journal write inside the handler makes both the event and the implicit 'this seq is processed' marker durable before the ACK. A crash before the commit means the producer retransmits and the journal-side dedup catches the re-run; a crash after the commit but before the ACK arrives means the dedup short-circuits and the controller acks at once. Either way, no duplication.

nodes.label: Crash between processing and ACK
nodes.rationale: The ACK never reaches the producer, which retransmits after resendTimeoutMs; the controller's in-memory dedup is gone after the crash, so the handler runs again for the same seq — make it idempotent or persist the processed seq alongside the business state.

nodes.label: ConfirmationCallback (producer-side confirm)
nodes.rationale: confirm(null) fires exactly once, after the consumer's ACK reached the producer and the in-flight slot is free; a redelivered duplicate ACK for the same seq is ignored so the callback never double-fires. It is the ONLY producer-side signal that a message arrived — without it the send is fire-and-forget as far as your code is concerned.

nodes.label: ReliableDelivery facade
nodes.rationale: ReliableDelivery.producer returns a ProducerHandle whose tell(body, confirm?) takes the optional confirmation callback; ReliableDelivery.consumer wraps the consumer side.

nodes.label: Sharded consumers need persistent dedup
nodes.rationale: When the consumer entity moves at failover the new instance starts with an empty in-memory dedup state, so without a persisted processed seq every rebalance means full reprocessing.

nodes.label: Slow-consumer backpressure
nodes.rationale: Once windowSize unacked messages are in flight the producer stops sending and incoming sends queue inside it — the system cannot outrun itself by more than the flow-control window.
